name: Personality maxxing / interests

lead: Personality maxxing means working on the non-physical side of attractiveness: humor, conversation, confidence, hobbies and interests.
People pair it with physical improvements, on the view that being engaging and interesting adds to how attractive someone is seen to be.

paras: It works through impressions: more skills, interests and social ease change how a person comes across in person.
It is a low-risk lifestyle practice; no formal research exists under this name.

chain: Develop hobbies, skills and social ease
Come across as more confident, interesting and engaging
Greater perceived attractiveness beyond looks alone
angle.text: Personality maxxing works through impressions rather than appearance itself: people who are engaging, relaxed and interesting in person are described by proponents as being seen as more attractive, and good-looking people in the community use it to round out their physical work.

lead: Personality maxxing is the looksmaxxing-community term for improving the non-physical side of attractiveness: social skills, humor, confidence, hobbies, interests and general presence. Proponents treat it as a complement to facial and body work, on the view that how a person comes across in conversation and what they do with their life adds to how attractive they are seen to be.

Typical activities discussed under the label include building skills and hobbies, becoming more socially fluent, improving conversation and humor, developing a style and cultivating interests that make a person more interesting to others. The practice is a lifestyle approach rather than a product or procedure, and no formal research programme exists under this name.

paras: The term follows the community habit of adding the suffix -maxxing to any area people try to optimize. Here the area is personality and interests rather than face or body.

Proponents say that attractiveness is perceived as a whole, so charisma, humor and shared interests can raise how appealing someone seems, and that interests and skills give people confidence and things to talk about. These are community beliefs.
Within the community, personality work is usually presented as a companion to physical improvement and as something available to everyone at little cost.
